author: ChatGPT
method: Individually authored kit objectives, item interactions, falsifications and matched-condition tests.

builds.name: Reference: Ranked support core
builds.goal: Reference for Thresh: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ support players use most (8,192 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 59.9% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A catch-and-peel controller who hooks enemies, adjusts spacing with Flay and offers allies a lantern escape while souls grow defenses and AP. The current support provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow → Zeke's Convergence. Aftershock keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Boots of Swiftness, Celestial Opposition, Bandlepipes.
builds.summary: The proven support baseline: Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow → Zeke's Convergence, with Aftershock.
testPlan: Play it in support as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow → Zeke's Convergence) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 59.9% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow → Zeke's Convergence.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
Thresh throws out his scythe, Stunning the first unit hit and Pulling them towards Thresh for [1.5] seconds. The scythe does [100 / 150 / 200 / 250 / 300 + (0.9) × AP] magic damage and also grants True Sight for the duration.

Thresh can Recast this Ability to pull himself to the enemy.

If this Ability hits, its Cooldown is reduced by [2] seconds.

Thresh throws his lantern, allowing an ally to click on it to dash to Thresh.

The lantern also grants [50 / 70 / 90 / 110 / 130 + (2) × BuffStacks({5fbfbf13})] Shield for [4] seconds to Thresh and the first ally champion to come in contact with it.

Passive: Thresh's Attacks deal additional damage based on how long since he last Attacked. They deal between [(1.7) × BuffStacks({5fbfbf13})] and [(1.7) × BuffStacks({5fbfbf13}) + (0.9 / 1.2 / 1.5 / 1.8 / 2.1) × AD] magic damage.

Active: Thresh whips his chains, Pulling or Pushing enemies in the direction of the swing. Enemies hit are also Slowed by [20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40]% for [1] second and take [65 / 110 / 155 / 200 / 245 + (0.6) × AP] magic damage.
Thresh collects the Souls of dead enemies by walking near them. Each Soul grants him [1] Armor and [1] Ability Power.

Thresh creates a prison of spectral walls, Slowing champions by [99]% for [2] seconds and dealing [250 / 400 / 550 + (1) × AP] magic damage. Walls break after one collision, and after one is broken, the rest deal no damage and Slow for half duration.

builds.name: Damage interaction: AD charged-Flay ambush
builds.goal: Maximize the first fully charged E-passive attack
builds.summary: Maximize the first fully charged E-passive attack.
builds.hypothesis: At rank 5 the stored Flay passive adds up to 210% total AD plus a soul term as MAGIC damage. High AD strengthens that packet; Void Staff addresses its MR mitigation. RFC tests attack access. Crit/Infinity Edge affect the normal physical attack, not automatically the Flay magic packet. Essence Reaver is another separately measured packet.
testPlan: Fix 80 souls and wait for full E charge. Compare the first hit with immediate second/third attacks; repeat at 50/150 MR and 50/150 armor. Replace RFC with Youmuu at matched gold to compare access with AD.
Use three repeatable trials at the same level, ranks, gold spent, target HP/armor/MR and incoming damage. Record the short trade and ten-second fight separately.

Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. First Strike must be ready and initiated by you; Gathering Storm uses a fixed recorded game time. Do not grant full ramp, transformed items or takedown bonuses for free.
Repeat with a moving opponent and real interruption. Compare the reference route at the same cost; log missed actions and survival as well as damage.
failureConditions: The opponent prevents the opening attack, or repeated attacks are mistakenly credited with full charge. Crit never multiplies the Flay packet in the measurement.
Higher stationary-target damage is offset by lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: This objective is deliberately narrower than the entire champion kit; an ability ceiling is not proof of a strong overall build.
Farmed-role experiments require actual income and a viable early lane/clear. A support comparison keeps quest/vision responsibility.
Item/rune/pet/empowered-attack proc compatibility must be observed rather than inferred from a shared damage type.
buyOrder: Farming-role experiment: early AD/Spellblade checkpoint, then penetration for the actual target; keep boots. Compare Bloodthirster raw AD with a cheaper component stage.
Compare a two-item checkpoint before the late six-slot illustration. Preserve movement boots unless a measured late replacement improves delivered damage.
coverageNotes: No numerical adapter exists for this champion. These individually authored hypotheses need manual game measurements; no global damage optimum or historical novelty is claimed.
Stored patch 26.20 source formulas are evidence, not a certified executable simulation. Resolve ambiguous tokens/stat formulas and current proc interactions before assigning numerical damage.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Armored soul collector
builds.goal: Turn fixed soul armor into repeated rescue opportunities
builds.summary: Turn fixed soul armor into repeated rescue opportunities.
builds.hypothesis: Damnation gives armor and AP per earned soul, while W shielding uses the soul count directly. Frozen Heart targets attack pressure; mana enables repeated actions but is not an extra lantern ratio. This route asks whether staying alive creates a second useful W or E, rather than optimizing a damage screenshot.
testPlan: Test at 40 and 80 earned souls without changing items. Use a physical attack opponent then magic burst. Count completed rescues, second E casts, mana spent and time until death.
Use three repeatable trials at the same level, ranks, gold spent, target HP/armor/MR and incoming damage. Record the short trade and ten-second fight separately.

Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. First Strike must be ready and initiated by you; Gathering Storm uses a fixed recorded game time. Do not grant full ramp, transformed items or takedown bonuses for free.
Repeat with a moving opponent and real interruption. Compare the reference route at the same cost; log missed actions and survival as well as damage.
failureConditions: Magic burst bypasses the armor emphasis; more survival creates no extra useful rescue or control.
Higher stationary-target damage is offset by lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: This objective is deliberately narrower than the entire champion kit; an ability ceiling is not proof of a strong overall build.
Farmed-role experiments require actual income and a viable early lane/clear. A support comparison keeps quest/vision responsibility.
Item/rune/pet/empowered-attack proc compatibility must be observed rather than inferred from a shared damage type.
buyOrder: Support quest/boots first; Frozen Heart only for actual attack pressure; add ally protection at realistic support income.
Compare a two-item checkpoint before the late six-slot illustration. Preserve movement boots unless a measured late replacement improves delivered damage.

builds.name: Experiment: Soul-powered on-hit carry
builds.goal: Test repeated soul-based attacks against the charged-hit route
builds.summary: Test repeated soul-based attacks against the charged-hit route.
builds.hypothesis: The uncharged Flay passive retains its soul term even when the AD charge is empty. Nashor and attack speed may make repeat hits relevant; soul AP also supports spells. Guinsoo extra on-hits must be observed separately: do not assume another fully charged Flay, E cast or crit on each phantom hit.
testPlan: Fix 80 souls; compare a fully charged first attack plus six seconds of attacks with the AD ambush. Repeat at zero souls. Isolate Guinsoo on-hit behavior before granting duplicated passive damage.
Use three repeatable trials at the same level, ranks, gold spent, target HP/armor/MR and incoming damage. Record the short trade and ten-second fight separately.

Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. First Strike must be ready and initiated by you; Gathering Storm uses a fixed recorded game time. Do not grant full ramp, transformed items or takedown bonuses for free.
Repeat with a moving opponent and real interruption. Compare the reference route at the same cost; log missed actions and survival as well as damage.
failureConditions: High soul count hides an unusable early build; attack access or lantern positioning is worse than the support control.
